_doc: First-person presentation (ADR-0029). Read by the arms generator (tools/assetgen/blender/lib/char_fp.py bakes one fp_* action per hold pose, attack and use) and by ViewModel at runtime. Positions and directions are in camera space (x right, y up, z back; metres). A hand spec places the hand by its grip: 'grip' point, 'dir' (handle axis, thumb side), 'knuckles' (where the knuckles point), 'fist' / 'thumb' curl 0..1 (fist 1 closes round a ~3.5 cm handle, up to 1.3 a bare fist), 'index' extra index curl (-1 points), optional 'curls' {finger: curl} (fingers index, middle, ring, pinky) closing those fingers to their own curl instead of the fist (for the index, instead of fist + index), e.g. a knife held with the little finger off the handle: 'curls': {'ring': 0.9, 'pinky': 0.4}, 'elbow' hint added to the rest elbow direction; or {'on': 'R', 'along': m, 'spin': deg} grips the other hand's handle. Attack and use keys are [frame, channels, ease] with channels relative to the hold: S.move [x,y,z] m, S.rot [pitch, yaw, roll] deg about the camera axes (pivot on the grip), S.elbow, S.along, S.spin and the curls (S.fist, S.thumb, S.index, S.flick, and S.curls {finger: curl}, which overrides those fingers for that key while the rest keep the hold's own; a finger with its own curl at either key eases between what it closes to at each). Edit, then `python tools/build_assets.py --match fp_arms` and import. A hold or an attack/use may set 'fixed_roll': ['R'] (sides) to keep the authored roll of those fists about what they hold (a gun's barrel, an inspect's turn-over); otherwise PoseSolver may roll a fist about its handle to spare the wrist. An attack/use without one inherits its hold's.

wrist._doc: A wrist's range (degrees, ADR-0045): flexion, extension, radial and ulnar deviation (an ellipse between them) and the forearm's roll either way of the thumb-up rest. PoseSolver keeps every baked hand inside it (the elbow swings to line the forearm up first, then the hand turns back about its grip); test_viewmodel_holds checks the baked arms.

defaults._doc: Hold class of an item without equip.hold: by equip.kind, then (melee) by damage_type, then by category. use_by_category picks the use action for consumables.

empty._doc: Bare hands: loose fists at the lower edge, ready.

one_hand._doc: Axes, hatchet, machete, hammer: carried low at the right, the head forward and in, edge leading (the knuckles' side); the handle crosses the palm obliquely (item rot: 25 degrees toward the knuckles, as a fist really closes on a haft), so the wrist can drive the head down. The off hand drops below the view.

club._doc: Stone club, steel pipe: both hands on the haft (the left below the right), carried low in front with the head up and in; the haft crosses the right palm obliquely (item rot) so the wrists can bring the head down onto the target.

spear._doc: Spear: low at the right hip, point forward to the centre. The shaft lies diagonally across the rear palm (item rot: 60 degrees about the palm's normal, an oblique grip), so the wrist can hold it forward; the front hand under the shaft follows the shaft, not the socket (ADR-0045).

two_hand._doc: Shovel: carried ready to dig, the rear fist overhand on the butt at the right hip and the shaft running down and forward past the centre, blade low in front; the front hand under the shaft. The shaft lies across the rear palm (item rot: 60 degrees about the palm's normal, an oblique grip as the spear's), so the blade can point down without the wrist bending past its range (TD-172).

light_left._doc: Torch, flashlight, lighter: held up in the left hand, the right hand loose and ready.

flashlight._doc: Flashlight: overhand in the left fist, the lens out of the little-finger side so the beam goes where you look; the forearm crosses the lower left. The right hand loose and ready.

pistol._doc: Revolver: one-handed low ready in the right fist, barrel forward and a little in, canted a touch so the cylinder shows; the index lies straight along the frame over the trigger guard (on the trigger only to fire). item rot z follows the grip's 15 degree rake so the fist closes along the grip, high under the hammer. The off hand is down out of view; it comes up to reload.

held._doc: Anything small carried on the right palm: resources, medicine, placeables, stones.

food._doc: A can, a bar, a mushroom: in the right fist, ready to eat.

bottle._doc: A bottle upright in the right fist.

blueprint._doc: Laying out a blueprint: the Field Manual open on the left palm, the right hand pointing.

carry_log._doc: A log on the right shoulder: its front end rises out of the top right; the right hand steadies it from below, the left hangs free.

lighter._doc: Lighter: upright in the left hand at chest height, fingers round its body, the thumb over the wheel and the flame up and a little forward; the right hand down out of view.

knife._doc: Knives: low at the right in a hammer grip, the point forward and a little up toward the centre, the edge down (an axe's upright carry read wrong on a kitchen knife). Quick forehand slice.

rifle._doc: Bolt-action rifle (ADR-0057): a two-handed long gun at the low ready, the stock in the right shoulder's line, the barrel forward and a touch in. The gun lies in the LEFT fist under the fore-end (hand: L; item rot turns its pointing frame onto the palm, scaled to 0.85 so it fits the arms' reach), so the right hand is free to leave the wrist of the stock and work the bolt; every right-hand key is placed on the gun where it is at that key (tools: scratchpad rifle_vm.py). No tether reading with it up (both hands busy). aim: the scope's ocular (socket_sight) comes up onto the line of sight 7 cm before the eye; the scope picture takes over from there.

attacks._doc: fp_<name>: played over the item's attack_time, so `impact` (the hit resolves at attack_time x impact) sits on the keyed contact frame.

fire_pistol._doc: A shot: on top of the procedural recoil, the muzzle flips and the wrist soaks it up, back on aim in a quarter second; the index on the trigger, then back along the frame.

reload_pistol._doc: Reload (played over equip.reload_time): the gun comes in and rolls left, the off hand comes up under it, the cylinder swings out (parts: the revolver's `cylinder` node about its crane, deg, keyed in frames), muzzle up and a slap on the ejector rod, muzzle down, the thumb presses three pairs of rounds home, the cylinder snaps shut and the gun goes back to the ready.

inspect_pistol._doc: Look it over (Y): the revolver comes in and turns to show its right side, then rolls over to show the left and the cylinder, and goes back to the ready.

fire_rifle._doc: A shot and the bolt (played over equip.attack_time + bolt_time): the rifle bucks up and back into the shoulder, then rolls a little onto its left side and comes up while the right hand goes from the wrist to the bolt knob: up, back (the empty flies), forward, down, and back to the wrist. parts: the rifle's `bolt` node, turned about the bore (deg) and slid along it (m).

reload_rifle_open._doc: Reload, first: the rifle rolls onto its left side and comes up, the right hand lifts the bolt and draws it back (equip.reload_open_time).

reload_rifle._doc: Reload, each round (equip.reload_time, repeated up to the magazine): the right hand drops for a round, brings it over the open action and thumbs it down, back to the bolt knob. The bolt stays open (parts).

reload_rifle_close._doc: Reload, last: the bolt runs forward and turns down, the right hand goes back to the wrist and the rifle to the ready (equip.reload_close_time).

inspect_rifle._doc: Look it over (Y): the rifle comes up and in, rolls onto its left side to show the bolt and the scope's turrets, then tips the muzzle up and across to look along the top and the left of the stock, and back to the ready; the right hand stays on the wrist.

tether._doc: Raising the left wrist to read the tether (T): the reading pose, how long the raise and lower take, the viewmodel's narrower field of view while reading (the screen fills more of the view), and the screen's glow lowered / raised.

guard._doc: Holding Block with a melee weapon raises the hold's guard: a blow from within arc_deg of where you face loses the hold's (or equip.block's) share of its damage, costing stamina per blocked hit plus per point absorbed. You can't attack while guarding.

aim._doc: Aiming a gun (right mouse, ADR-0057): seconds to raise it (time), the view's magnification when up (zoom), multipliers on spread, the arms' sway and walking speed when up, and from what fraction of the raise a scoped gun shows its scope picture. Per item, equip.aim overrides these (the rifle's 4x scope, the revolver's iron sights); where the gun sits when up is its hold's `aim` (the sight socket, its height above it, how far before the eye, the arms' field of view).

motion._doc: Procedural motion on top of the baked poses. breathe: period s, pos m, rot deg. sway: the rig lags the view (deg of lag per rad/s of turn), sprung. move: lag against velocity changes. bob: per footstep (pos m, rot deg), scaled when sprinting / crouched. sprint: the lowered pose (pos m, rot deg) blended in while sprinting. land: dip per m/s of landing speed. equip: seconds to raise a new item.

impact._doc: Feedback when a swing connects, by what it hit: hitstop (s the swing freezes), camera kick (pitch, yaw, roll deg; sprung back), rig recoil (m), and particles where the target makes none of its own.

stagger._doc: Taking a hit knocks the arms: deg and m per point of damage, capped; a blocked hit jolts the guard instead.

_doc_off_hand: Holds that use one hand drop the other below the view (it comes up to guard or read the tether): the owner's playtest found an open hand floating palm-down in the lower corner distracting.
